title: POC weekly: model catalog contrast & degraded-paths sync
topics: version pinning workflow and rollback windows
soft fallback paths and canary behavior
latency vs cost tradeoff for production routes
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on choosing a model variant to pin for the next pilot week, reviewing recent run summary metrics, and defining tolerant rollback/fallback behavior. Customer asked for clearer canary rules, auditability for changes, and a short checklist for degraded-path routing. Redwood AE+SE proposed 13B quantized as primary with 7B as a cold fallback for burst pressure; customer to validate latency/cost spreadsheet and security docs.
next_steps: Priya to run targeted 1k prompt latency+cost sweep comparing 13B q4 and 7B q2 quant profiles and share spreadsheet by 2025-11-24
Alex to send updated runbook with soft-rollback playbook and canary gating rules by 2025-11-20
Maria to confirm pilot success criteria and internal stakeholders by 2025-11-21
Rafael to provide list of compliance artifacts needed for dedicated/private evaluation by 2025-11-25
action_items: Priya Shah - run 1,000 prompt latency/cost comparison (13B quant vs 7B quant) - due 2025-11-24
Alex Carter - draft soft rollback runbook (includes traffic split thresholds, error rate triggers, automatic fallback endpoints) - due 2025-11-20
Maria Velasquez - confirm success criteria and add product PM to next call - due 2025-11-21
Rafael Mendes - enumerate required SOC2/ISO docs and KMS questions for private deployment - due 2025-11-25
meeting_header: Date: 2025-11-18 | Start: 15:30 PST | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maria Velasquez (Cortex MLOps), Tom Hsu (Cortex Backend), Rafael Mendes (Cortex Security)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Okay welcome everyone, thanks for joining our weekly POC sync, um we have about 50 minutes so we'll run through results, proposed pinning, and fallback playbook.
[00:12] Maria: Thanks Alex, we had a busy week on the eval side, saw some interesting latency spikes on the 13B runs but cost looked favorable, we'll share the raw logs.
[00:22] Priya: Quick note, the spikes you saw sound like batching mismatch—when sequence length distribution changed the autoscaler pulled in extra workers and that introduced queuing, so it looked like a model issue but it's infra-behavior.
[00:34] Tom: Yeah we observed queuing, and some of our endpoints have unpredictable token lengths because of long user messages.
[00:40] Alex: Right, so first agenda item: model selection. Our recommendation this week was to try pinning a 13B quantized variant for the primary route and keep 7B quantized as a cold fallback. The tradeoff is better quality at slightly higher median latency.
[00:55] Maria: Can you remind us of the quant profiles again, Priya? q2 vs q4? I'm mixing them up.
[01:02] Priya: Sure, we ran 7B with q2 and 13B with q4 int8-ish profile. The 13B q4 tends to give more coherent completions on long-context prompts, especially for multi-step extraction tasks. 7B q2 is cheaper and lower latency but occasionally fails hallucination checks.
[01:18] Maria: Okay that jibes with the evals. The quality delta matters for our NER cascades.
[01:24] Rafael: From security side we want to make any rollback path auditable — who changed the pin, when, and what triggered it.
[01:32] Alex: Absolutely, we can include audit-log entries for pin changes in the runbook. Our control plane records actor, timestamp, and reason but we'll add explicit runbook instructions for when to pin/unpin.
[01:45] Tom: On canary gates — what's the recommended traffic split? We want something conservative but actionable.
[01:50] Priya: Typical pattern we use: start with 1% traffic to the new pin for 30 minutes, monitor latency p50/p95, error rate, and model-quality evals against a prompt set. If metrics stable, increase to 10% for 2 hours, then 50% for the rest of the day before full roll. For POCs, you can shorten windows but keep the same thresholds.
[02:12] Maria: Do you support automatic fallback if error rate crosses threshold?
[02:15] Alex: Yes we have automated fallback policies — you can configure error-rate and latency triggers. We'll send you the standard policy but also include a 'soft' fallback that redirects to 7B and keeps the traffic on the same route but with lower cost.
[02:29] Rafael: Important: any automated fallback must emit an audit event and we need to retain that in our logs. Also KMS key usage for model telemetry needs to be documented.
[02:38] Priya: Noted, we'll include KMS access logs sample.
[02:42] Tom: Quick question on prefix caching / KV cache, is it preserved across fallback? Because we saw cold starts when we switched between variants.
[02:50] Priya: Good call — prefix cache isn't compatible across different model architectures or quantization profiles, so when you fallback between 13B and 7B you'll likely see KV cache misses; that explains the cold latency. We're working on transparent cache warmers but for now expect a short penalty on switch.
[03:10] Maria: So that suggests we should prefer soft-rollback where we route new requests to fallback but keep existing sessions on primary until they finish?
[03:16] Alex: Exactly — sticky sessions and drain behavior minimize user-visible regressions. We'll detail drain windows in the runbook.
[03:22] Tom: On the benchmark results — we got a CSV from you, but some columns look truncated; could you re-run with absolute token counts (input/output) and per-request walltime?
[03:30] Priya: Yep we'll reformat. Also we'll add percentiles and median and the cost per request based on your token mix.
[03:36] Maria: Regarding model pins, what's the recommended duration to hold a pin in pilot? If we pin for too long and then new model drops, how do we avoid tech debt?
[03:45] Alex: Good question. For pilots we recommend pin windows of 1-2 weeks with scheduled evaluation at 72-hour and 1-week marks. If a new model variant is released you can create a canary from it rather than flipping the pin immediately.
[03:58] Rafael: From compliance, we need a change freeze window before any production roll: a checklist and sign-off by SRE and Security. Can you provide a template?
[04:07] Alex: Yes we'll include a sign-off template in the runbook, with the required fields (owner, rollback plan, metrics checked).
[04:14] [crosstalk] Tom: (inaudible) — also want to check network egress if we move to dedicated.
[04:20] Priya: For Dedicated, egress stays in your VPC in Private deployments, and for Redwood Dedicated we can restrict egress via peering and firewall rules. We'll include network diagrams.
[04:30] Maria: On the latency spikes, is there a way to simulate sequence-length distribution that mimics live traffic for the benchmark?
[04:36] Priya: Yes we can replay a sampled set of 5k requests from your logs — that will give a more accurate p95 than synthetic uniform tests. Please send a sanitized sample and we'll run it.
[04:46] Maria: We'll anonymize and send.
[04:48] Alex: Next topic: degraded-paths naming. We call them fallback, soft-rollback, and emergency route. I'd like to confirm your preference because docs use inconsistent names.
[04:56] Maria: Let's standardize on fallback (planned), soft-rollback (automatic with warm switch), and emergency-redirect (manual hot switch).
[05:05] Alex: Noted. We'll align runbook.
[05:08] Priya: Also a small gotcha—if you use model variants with different vocab/tokenizer versions there can be subtle output differences; keep an eye on tokenization drift.
[05:17] Tom: Oof, tokenizer drift caused us some issues before. Good call.
[05:20] Rafael: Security quick question — where are logs stored for the pinned model change events? Retention policy?
[05:25] Alex: We store audit logs in your configured logging sink (Cloud Logging / SIEM), with retention configurable per account. Default is 90 days, but enterprise plans can extend.
[05:34] Rafael: We need 365 days for compliance.
[05:36] Alex: That's possible; we'll note that in the proposal.
[05:39] Maria: Can we get an example of the rollback condition syntax? Like a rule we can paste into our tooling?
[05:44] Priya: Yes — an example: if route.p95_latency > 1500ms for 10m OR error_rate > 2% over 5m then trigger soft-rollback; we'll send the JSON/YAML snippet but in this call quick example is that.
[05:58] Tom: We use Prometheus for metrics; will alerts integrate?
[06:02] Alex: We can emit metrics to Prometheus or cloud monitoring; integrations are supported.
[06:07] Maria: One more ask — during canary, how do we evaluate model quality? We need automated checks beyond basic metrics.
[06:13] Priya: We can run a prompt-based quality eval against a golden prompt set and surface drift metrics (F1/NER score, hallucination heuristics). For the POC we'll run the golden set every 30 mins during canary. That will be in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:28] Maria: Sounds good.
[06:30] Alex: Alright let's recap: Priya runs the 1k/5k replays with tokenized counts and writes up a cost/latency spreadsheet; Alex will draft the runbook with canonical names and soft-rollback playbook; Maria will confirm success criteria/PM; Rafael will list compliance artifacts.
[06:47] Rafael: Also please include KMS key rotation policy notes if we're evaluating private.
[06:53] Priya: We'll add KMS rotation and HSM notes.
[07:00] [15 minute mark — middle of call continues with deeper technical dive]
[07:10] Priya: Looking at the logs from last week one more note — the autoscaler scales on GPU utilization which sometimes overprovisions if you have bursty small requests; consider request-based concurrency limits per worker in addition to CPU/GPU thresholds.
[07:26] Tom: How does request concurrency interact with batching? We don't want small requests to starve large ones.
[07:31] Priya: We partition batches by priority and sequence-length buckets; smaller requests can be batched together but we also reserve a fraction of slots for long-sequence tasks. It's configurable in the route policy.
[07:45] Maria: That seems useful — maybe we start with a 20% reserved for long tasks.
[07:50] Alex: We'll include recommended defaults.
[07:53] [crosstalk — 2 people talking]
[08:00] Tom: On pins, is there an API? We prefer infra-as-code changes rather than manual console fiddling.
[08:05] Alex: Yes we have both — an API and CLI that support model pin creation, history, and rollbacks. Pins are auditable and you can script the canary windows.
[08:14] Maria: We'll want an example Terraform snippet.
[08:17] Alex: We'll provide one.
[08:19] Priya: One possible gotcha: if you pin and then later pin a model that gets updated in-place (same model name different binary) you might not get what you expected; we recommend pinning exact model-version hashes when you need determinism.
[08:34] Maria: Good to know.
[08:36] Alex: Closing questions?
[08:38] Maria: None from me. We'll send the sample logs by EOD tomorrow.
[08:42] Tom: I'll loop in the PM and SRE as requested.
[08:46] Rafael: We'll confirm the compliance doc list by next week.
[08:49] Alex: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the spreadsheet and runbook links, and schedule next check-in for 2025-11-25 same time.
[08:58] [end]
